newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra, Victoria, BHP, Esso settle dispute.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra, Victoria, BHP, Esso settle dispute.

text.p: The Australian Federal government, the state of Victoria and Bass Strait gas producers, The Broken Hill Pty Ltd and Exxon Corp, had settled their long running dispute over Petroleum Resource Rent Tax, Treasurer Peter Costello said.

The settlement will give the Federal government an unbudgeted gain of A$70 million in a round-robin of payments from Canberra to Victoria, to the producers and back to Canberra, a Treasury official told Reuters.

The dispute centres on a Federal tax that the producers sought to pass on to their customers, Victorian government utilities. If Victoria paid the tax, that would have amounted to a revenue stream that the Federal government would have taxed -- effectively giving it the windfall of tax on tax.
In fact, no money changed hands until now.

The Treasury official said the Federal government will pay back to Victoria the windfall of A$550 million, Victoria will pay an agreed amount representing its obligation to the producers, and the producers will pay an amount into the tax office.
The A$70 million boost to the Federal government stemmed from the transition from the previous resource rent scheme to the current one, he said.
The parties had agreed that Canberra was entitled to this money, he said.
The settlement, to be authorised by a special appropriations act from the Federal parliament, will take place on November 29.
Esso Australia Resources Ltd is a subsidiary of Exxon Corp.
